burton_span.exact: a knave will be a knave

source.author: Horace
source.basis: Burton does not name the source. This is Horace's well-known line on nature and the pitchfork, "Naturam expelles furca, tamen usque recurret", and Burton's wording is almost the same.

2.3.7.1-f52.text: Naturam expellas furca licet usque recurret

translations.literal: You may drive out nature with a fork, although it will always run back.
translations.note: Horace's line reads "Naturam expelles furca, tamen usque recurret". Burton's version has "expellas … licet" instead of "expelles … tamen", but the sense is the same. In the main text, Burton's "a knave will be a knave" gives the moral of the line in proverbial form rather than translating it.
